summary: The glean CLI (gleanwork/glean-cli) is the vendor-published, agent-friendly command-line client for Glean enterprise search, chat, agents, and knowledge management, wrapping the Client API in three tiers (raw glean api, typed namespace commands, and ergonomic search/chat). Hands-on verification against a live authenticated tenant (v0.17.1) confirmed the documented capability map but surfaced several undocumented gotchas: --dry-run only previews a request's body (not full request detail, unlike --preview), chat --save defaults to true, the CLI is single-tenant with no profile support, search has no recency-sort flag, and the credential-resolution fallback (env to keyring to config file) does not fully account for one observed case where auth succeeded despite all three sources appearing empty. Sourced from 2 files (1 developer reference, 1 hands-on research dossier) in the integration-clients hub.

facts.text: **The CLI is not read-only.** Write verbs exist across six namespaces: `answers create|delete|update`, `collections create|delete|add-items|delete-item|update`, `pins create|remove|update`, `shortcuts create|delete|update`, `announcements create|delete|update`, `verification remind|verify`, `activity feedback|report` [C-6]. Any automation given a Glean token can mutate shared tenant state — announcements and go-links are org-visible. This contradicts the common assumption (including in some local skill templates) that Glean access is inherently read-only.

**Concept:** the `glean` command-line interface, v0.17.1 **Run:** rabbithole, 2026-09-17 · primary source = live binary introspection + live API calls on tenant `mongodb-be.glean.com` **Scope-in:** the CLI itself — command surface, auth, flags, output contract, API mapping, pagination, error behaviour, scripting patterns. **Scope-out (ADJ):** the Glean platform (indexing/ranking/permissions), the Glean MCP server, the web UI, non-Go SDKs, tenant datasource configuration.

facts.text: `glean` is the vendor-published CLI for a Glean instance: an authenticated HTTP client over Glean's REST API, wrapped in three layers of increasing ergonomics, plus a machine-readable schema surface explicitly built for agent consumption rather than human documentation [C-1, C-7].

**Instance resolution is the `server_url` key, and there is exactly one of it** [C-19, C-22]. There is no `--instance` flag, no profile flag, and no profile structure in the config. **The CLI is single-tenant at a time**: switching Glean instances means re-running `auth login` and overwriting the one config. Anyone working across two tenants must swap `~/.glean/config.json` by hand or point `GLEAN_API_TOKEN` at the other instance.

Effective prompt patterns for Glean MCP: - State the data or action desired explicitly - Provide document links or IDs when available - Ask the assistant which tool it plans to use when debugging tool selection

1. Start with `glean schema` when unsure about a command. 2. Use `--dry-run` before write/delete operations — but see 3.7, it only shows the body. 3. Use `--fields` when you only need a subset of response fields. 4. Use `--output ndjson` for streaming or large-result workflows. 5. Keep secrets in env vars — never inline in committed scripts.

- For Chrome extension Glean integration patterns (auth cascade, tab-based session, MCP JSON-RPC flow): use `glean-llm-client-patterns` instead. - For general MCP protocol (not Glean-specific): use `mcp-servers`.

Workaround patterns when you need Glean-originated event notifications: 1. **Polling:** use the Insights API periodically 2. **Agent-based:** run agents on a schedule and process outputs 3. **CLI scripting:** use `glean` CLI in cron jobs

**Rate-limit and 429 behaviour is unverified.** Whether the CLI retries, backs off, or surfaces HTTP 429 raw is not established. The local `docs.glean.com` mirror discusses rate limits only for *Slack's* API as consumed by Glean's real-time search, not for Glean's own API as consumed by this CLI. Closing this honestly requires vendor documentation or deliberately hammering the API, which this run declined to do. Treat automation against this CLI as having unknown backoff semantics until tested.

- **The CLI is not read-only.** Write verbs exist across 6 of the 13 namespaces: `answers create|delete|update`, `collections create|delete|add-items|delete-item|update`, `pins create|remove|update`, `shortcuts create|delete|update`, `announcements create|delete|update`, `verification remind|verify`, `activity feedback|report`. Announcements and shortcuts (go-links) are org-visible — a script holding a token can mutate shared tenant state. - **`glean chat --save` defaults to `true`.** Scripted/agent `chat` calls write into the real Glean chat history unless you pass `--no-save`. **No indexing surface [C-23].** None of the 13 namespaces exposes datasource push / document indexing. Glean's API separates a user-scoped Client API from an admin-scoped Indexing API; this CLI (v0.17.1) appears to sit entirely on the client side. Stated as verified absence in this version, not as a claim about the API.

**Asymmetry worth knowing:** the CLI exposes no `--sort` flag, while Glean's MCP search tool exposes `sort_by_recency`. Recency-sorted search from the CLI requires hand-building the `--json` body [C-9].

`--save` **defaults to true** — scripted `glean chat` calls write into the user's real Glean chat history. The help text explicitly recommends `--no-save` "for agent/script use to avoid polluting history" [C-10]. Bare `glean` with no arguments opens a full-screen chat TUI; `--continue` resumes the most recent saved session [C-11].

`glean schema` lists 17 commands with registered schemas; `glean schema <cmd>` emits typed JSON (flag name, description, type, default). The help text states the purpose outright: for agents to call *before* invoking a command, "without needing documentation in context." This is an agent-first design decision, not an afterthought — it is the CLI's answer to tool-description bloat.

Pagination is cursor-based: responses carry a base64-encoded JSON `cursor` plus `hasMoreResults`; continuation goes back through a `--json` body, since no `--cursor` flag exists [C-9].

What exists: - **Inbound webhook receivers:** Glean consumes webhooks FROM external sources (HubSpot, Greenhouse, SharePoint) to keep its index current. - **Activity API (inbound):** `POST /rest/api/v1/activity` accepts events pushed TO Glean (requires ACTIVITY scope + global token).

1. **Indexing time:** documents pushed with permissions attached 2. **User/group resolution:** Glean resolves group memberships at query time 3. **Search time:** results filtered to documents the querying user can access 4. **Source ACL preservation:** Glean honors source system ACLs exactly 5. **IdP:** reads groups/members from IdPs but does NOT enforce IdP permission rules on document access
